topic: Discrete Convolutions: The Math of Blending and Shifting
target_audience: Undergraduate engineering and computer science students

sections.title: Introduction: The Concept of Merging Information
lecture_lines: Convolution merges two sequences into a new signal.
Imagine a clear Pixel Fox entering a foggy forest.
The fog's density modifies the fox's sharp image.
This interaction blends the data into a blurred output.
Mathematically, one signal influences another over time.
animations: Display two discrete sequences (blue #58C4DD bars and green #83C167 bars) that move towards each other and merge into a third purple #966FD6 sequence.
Show a clear [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg] on the screen.
Overlay a pattern of semi-transparent gray #A9A9A9 rectangles (representing fog) on top of the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg].
The [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg] transforms from sharp to a blurred version as the fog density interacts with it.
A transparent sliding window moves across a row of bars, with the average value being plotted as a new point above the window center.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Sequences and Flipping
lecture_lines: Discrete sequences represent data at specific points.
Convolution requires flipping the second sequence horizontally.
We transform the kernel sequence g[k] into g[-k].
animations: Display a set of vertical bars with heights [1, 2, 3] at integer positions, labeled as x[n] in white #FFFFFF.
The bars [1, 2, 3] rotate 180 degrees around the vertical axis at n=0 to become [3, 2, 1] in orange #FF8C00.
Display the original sequence and the flipped sequence side-by-side, with a 'Flip' arrow indicating the horizontal reversal.

sections.title: The Core Formula: Flip, Shift, Multiply, Sum
lecture_lines: The formula calculates how two signals interact.
First, flip the kernel sequence g[k] entirely.
Next, shift the flipped sequence by index n.
Multiply overlapping values at each sliding step.
Sum these products to find the output value.
animations: Write the formula $(f * g)[n] = \sum f[k]g[n-k]$ in white #FFFFFF at the top of the screen.
Sequence g[k] (red #FF6666 bars) is shown on an axis, then mirrored across the y-axis to become g[-k].
The flipped sequence g[-k] slides horizontally along the x-axis, with its position labeled as 'n'.
When bars from f[k] and the shifted g[n-k] overlap, they flash yellow #F9D71C and their product appears above them.
The product values move together and sum into a single bar, which is then placed at position 'n' in the output sequence.

sections.title: Graphical Interpretation: The Sliding Window
lecture_lines: Visualize a filter window sliding across a stationary signal.
The overlapping area determines the output at each index.
This sliding process creates a modified version of data.
animations: A stationary signal f[k] (blue #58C4DD) is shown while a filter g[n-k] (yellow #F9D71C) slides over it from left to right inside a window [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/window.svg].
The overlapping region between the signal and filter is filled with a bright color, and a vertical line indicates the current output value.
As the filter slides, a new, smoother sequence is drawn point-by-point below the main graph.

sections.title: Application: Image Processing and Blurring
lecture_lines: In 2D, images are grids of discrete pixel values.
A small matrix, or kernel, slides over these pixels.
Blurring replaces pixels with a weighted average of neighbors.
The Pixel Fox becomes soft as the kernel spreads data.
Convolutional networks use this to identify complex features.
animations: Zoom into a 5x5 grid of pixels on the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg], each square labeled with a numeric intensity value in white #FFFFFF.
A 3x3 red frame (#FF0000) slides across the 5x5 grid, pausing at the center pixel.
Inside the 3x3 frame, show the center pixel color changing to the average of its 8 neighbors to represent blurring.
The kernel values change to an edge-detection filter, and high-contrast boundaries in the grid start to glow white #FFFFFF.
The grid transforms into an abstract 'Feature Map' of the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fox.svg] where specific patterns (like a 'V' shape) are highlighted in cyan #00FFFF.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Convolution is essentially a weighted local average.
It is a vital tool for signal processing and AI.
This simple operation shapes our digital world.

Icons for a digital signal (oscilloscope) [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/oscill.svg] and a neural network (nodes and edges) fade in and out in cyan #00FFFF.
